specification.problem: Quantized density classification: a Quantum Particle Automata (QPA) evolves under a unitary operator U (parameterized by theta), and after measurement the particle's position basis state falls on one side of a boundary partition, deciding whether a length-5 binary input has majority 0 or majority 1. A Genetic Algorithm searches for U and the boundary partition.
specification.reconstruction_scope: Finite instance with binary input length n=5 only; the abstract states that scaling to arbitrary n is future work. The exact form of U, the encoding of inputs into the QPA state, and the GA details are not given in the abstract.

symbols.domain: positive integer; n=5 in the study

symbols.meaning: Unitary operator driving the QPA evolution, found by the GA
symbols.domain: unitary matrix on the particle position space

symbols.meaning: Parameter of U controlling the particle's effective mass and evolution speed
Boundary partition of basis states used to decide the majority
symbols.domain: partition of basis states into two sets

equations.label: Evolution
equations.description: QPA state after t evolution steps under the unitary operator U
equations.justification: The abstract says the QPA needs a unitary operator for its evolution; the power form is an assumed standard discrete-time model.
assumptions: Discrete time steps with the same U applied at each step

equations.label: Decision rule
equations.latex: P_1=\sum_{x\in B_1}|\langle x|\psi_t\rangle|^2,\quad \text{decide majority 1 if } P_1>1/2
equations.description: Probability that the measured particle lands on the side B_1 of the boundary partition; used to decide the majority density
equations.justification: The abstract says the particle is more likely to collapse to basis states on the correct side of the boundary partition; the threshold 1/2 is assumed.
assumptions: B_1 is the side associated with majority 1

registers.name: particle
registers.size: unknown (position space dimension not given; assumed at least 2^5=32 basis states if inputs are encoded as positions)
registers.role: QPA particle position register holding the encoded input and evolving under U

specification.initial_state: Assumed: |psi_0> is the particle prepared in the basis state (or superposition) encoding the length-5 binary input; the encoding is not given in the abstract.

steps.description: Encode the length-5 binary input into the initial particle state |psi_0>.
Apply the GA-found unitary U (parameterized by theta) for t steps to evolve the particle.
Compute the probability mass on each side of the GA-found boundary partition, to be used for the decision.

specification.measurement: Measure the particle position in the computational (position) basis after the evolution. The outcome x is assigned to one side of the GA-found boundary partition B; the side containing x gives the decision (majority 0 or majority 1). Success probability is the mass on the correct side (eq_2).
specification.classical_postprocessing: Compare the measured basis state to the boundary partition and output the majority label. Repeating the run and taking the majority of outcomes, or estimating P_1 and thresholding it, is an assumed option. The GA fitness would presumably be the correct-side probability over all 32 inputs (assumed; not stated).
assumptions: The equations are generic assumed models, not taken from the paper.
Register size and input encoding are assumed.
Particle register dimension and input encoding are assumed.
Measurement in the position basis and the 1/2 threshold are assumed.
missing_information: Exact form of U and its dependence on theta
Encoding of the binary input into the initial QPA state
Actual position space dimension of the QPA
Handling of ties for inputs of length 5 (none exist, since n is odd)
